model_comparison:
Both models successfully reproduced the text content without errors. However, their performance on the core paralinguistic task differed significantly.

Model 1 (T1) failed to execute the main instruction. It started with a low pitch as requested but maintained that low pitch throughout the entire sentence. There was no 'gradual transition to a medium pitch'. The slow, monotonous delivery also made it sound less natural.

Model 2 (T2), in stark contrast, executed the instruction almost perfectly. It began with a very low pitch on 'Look' (0:00-0:01) and then smoothly and gradually increased the pitch throughout the sentence. By the time it reached 'playing in the grass, so cute' (0:06-0:10), the pitch was clearly in a medium range, demonstrating a successful and noticeable transition. The progression felt natural and aligned with the sense of discovery in the text. 

The difference is significant. Model 2 understood and implemented the dynamic pitch change, whereas Model 1 only addressed the starting condition and failed to perform the transition. Therefore, Model 2 is the clear winner.
